identity.title: Probing the Relationship Between Early Star Formation and CO in the Dwarf Irregular Galaxy WLM with JWST

paper_type_evidence.quote: We utilize ALMA-detected CO cores, *JWST* near-infrared (NIR) images (F090W, F150W, F250M, and F430M), and *GALEX* far-ultraviolet (FUV) images of WLM

evidence.quote: Wolf-Lundmark-Melotte (WLM) is a nearby dwarf irregular galaxy (dIrr) in the Local Group at a distance of approximately 980 kpc (cite: Leaman_2012; Lee_2021).

question.value: How does early star formation (JWST NIR clumps) relate to CO cores and FUV in the low-metallicity dwarf irregular galaxy WLM?

evidence.quote: (2) the relationship between early star formation and CO in low metallicity environments.

For type 1 objects, 60% overlap 8 $\mu$m sources and 40% overlap $V$ sources
For type 2 objects, 15% overlap 8 $\mu$m sources and 48% overlap $V$ sources
For type 3 objects, 5% overlap 8 $\mu$m sources and 0% overlap $V$ sources
Type 1 objects range from approximately $1$ to $5930\ M_\odot$

findings_qualitative.value: Objects of all types have similar colors, magnitudes and temperatures

evidence.quote: We find that objects of all three types have comparable NIR colors and magnitudes.

claims.hypothesis: Objects near CO have different masses than objects away from CO
claims.experiment: Compared TIR-luminosity masses of three object types
claims.finding: Objects near CO are more massive, but PROSPECTOR masses show the same range for all types

evidence.quote: However, when the masses are measured using PROSPECTOR, all object types cover the same mass range.

claims.hypothesis: Objects near CO are embedded clusters at earlier stage
claims.finding: Suggestive of earlier embedded stage, but ages are required

evidence.quote: This suggests objects near CO may be embedded star clusters at an earlier stage of star formation, but accurate age estimates for all objects are required for confirmation.
